sources.design: Cochrane review of randomized or quasi-randomized UNE treatment trials.
sources.population: Clinical UNE; conservative evidence principally mild/moderate disease
sources.comparator: Information alone versus added splint/glides; other surgical/injection comparisons separate
sources.outcomes: Information may improve work/night pain as much as adding splint or glides; small/limited trials.
sources.followUp: Trial-specific; review and primary Svernlöv trial reports differ in analyzed denominator/timepoint account.
sources.uncertainty: Not adequate evidence for progressive motor deficits or all severity states.
sources.limitations: In clinically mild/moderate UNE, information alone may improve work activities/night pain as much as adding night splints or nerve glides; confidence limited by small trials/methods. Review cannot identify best therapy by severity/imaging/electrophysiology. It does not prove no conservative treatment works or that education is adequate for progressive motor deficits. Exercise dose and general gym restrictions are not established. Reported surgical comparisons do not answer exercise safety.

sources.title: Conservative treatment of the cubital tunnel syndrome
sources.publicationStatus: Final randomized study, Journal of Hand Surgery European Volume 2009;34(2):201–207.

access.details: Primary abstract and/or indexed source passages inspected; complete article inspection not established. [Primary abstract](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/19282413/). DOI 10.1177/1753193408098480; PMID 19282413. 70 mild/moderate patients received information about causes/avoiding provocation, randomized to information alone, night splint or nerve glides. Primary abstract: 57 followed at 6 months, 51 improved (89.5%), no significant group differences. Cochrane reports a smaller analyzed set; denominator/timepoint differences require preserving the source-specific account rather than merging. Night splint duration 3 months; exact glide repetition/hold dose not verified. Harms were not adequately reported. Not evidence that all exercise prevents surgery, nor that glides should be routine. Trial excluded several other upper-limb conditions; those exclusions are generalizability limits. Bounded accessible-protocol audit 2026-11-02: only explicitly reported categories/schedules entered; access status unchanged and exact unseen methods remain unreported.

sources.design: Prospective uncontrolled cohort, 19 patients and 25 extremities.
sources.coInterventions: Activity modification plus three months of rigid night splinting at 45° elbow flexion.
sources.outcomes: 21 of 24 available extremities avoided surgery (88%); QuickDASH improved from 29 to 11, grip from 32 to 35 kg.
sources.uncertainty: No control; splint angle not exercise limit; advice-only RCT did not show splint advantage.
sources.harms: Described well tolerated; comprehensive harm rate unavailable.
sources.limitations: 19 patients/25 extremities, mild–moderate idiopathic cubital tunnel syndrome. Activity modification plus rigid night splint at 45° elbow flexion for 3 months. At mean 2 years, 24 extremities available, 21 avoided surgery (88%); QuickDASH 29→11 and grip 32→35 kg. No control group; success defined by avoiding surgery, not confirmed reversal of nerve damage. Described well tolerated; no comprehensive harm rate. Night-splint angle is not an exercise elbow-flexion limit. Does not resolve whether splint adds benefit beyond advice, given UNE-P1.

sources.title: Changes in interstitial pressure and cross-sectional area of the cubital tunnel and of the ulnar nerve with flexion of the elbow. An experimental study in human cadavera.
sources.publicationStatus: Final cadaver experiment, Journal of Bone and Joint Surgery American Volume, April 1998;80(4):492–501.

access.details: Primary abstract and/or indexed source passages inspected; complete article inspection not established. [Primary abstract](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/9563378/). DOI 10.2106/00004623-199804000-00005; PMID 9563378. MRI and interstitial pressure while flexing human cadaver elbows. Tunnel/nerve area decreased toward 135°; intraneural pressure exceeded extraneural pressure at several flexed positions. No living clinical symptoms, exercise dose, longitudinal injury outcome or maximum safe angle. Mechanistic support for reducing sustained symptomatic flexion/pressure; not evidence for a universal 90° cap or no-flexion workouts. Bounded accessible-protocol audit 2026-11-02: only explicitly reported categories/schedules entered; access status unchanged and exact unseen methods remain unreported.
